body:
What does this print?

console.log(typeof 42);
explanation: JavaScript has a single numeric type for whole and decimal numbers, so typeof returns "number".

body: Which keyword declares a variable that cannot be reassigned?
explanation: A const binding cannot be reassigned after it is created. var and let can be reassigned.

body:
What does this print?

console.log("5" + 3);
explanation: When one side of + is a string, JavaScript joins the values as text, giving "53".

body:
What does this print?

console.log("5" - 3);
explanation: The - operator only works on numbers, so "5" is converted to 5 and 5 - 3 = 2.
length is the number of elements in the array: three.

body: Which array method adds an element to the end of an array?
explanation: push() appends to the end. pop() removes from the end; shift()/unshift() work at the start.

body:
What does this print?

console.log(3 === "3");
explanation: === compares both value and type. A number and a string are different types, so the result is false.

body: Which characters start a single-line comment in JavaScript?
explanation: // starts a comment that runs to the end of the line. # is used in Python, <!-- in HTML.
x += 2 means x = x + 2. Both are numbers, so x becomes 7.

body: Which built-in browser function shows a simple pop-up message to the user?
explanation: alert() shows a dialog with a message and an OK button. The other names are not built-in functions.

body:
What does this print?

console.log(0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3);
explanation: Decimal fractions are stored in binary floating point, so 0.1 + 0.2 is 0.30000000000000004, not exactly 0.3.

body:
What does this print?

console.log([1, 2, 3].map(n => n * 2));
explanation: map() returns a new array with the function applied to every element.

body:
What does this print?

console.log(typeof null);
explanation: typeof null returns "object". This is a long-standing quirk kept for backward compatibility.
A variable declared with let but not given a value holds undefined.
filter() keeps only the elements for which the function returns true: 12 and 21.

body:
What does this print?

console.log(Boolean(""));
explanation: An empty string is falsy, so converting it to a boolean gives false.
When no argument is passed, the default parameter value "Guest" is used.

body: What does document.getElementById("title") return when no element has that id?
explanation: getElementById returns null when nothing matches, so always check before using the result.
Object destructuring copies the property named city into a variable called city.

body:
What does this print?

console.log([..."abc"].reverse().join(""));
explanation: Spreading the string gives ["a","b","c"], reverse() flips it, and join("") glues it back into "cba".

body: Which statement about let and var is correct?
options: let is block-scoped; var is function-scoped
var is block-scoped; let is function-scoped
explanation: A let variable exists only inside the { } block where it is declared; a var variable belongs to the whole function.
setTimeout callbacks run only after the current code finishes, even with a 0 ms delay, so 2 is printed last.
var creates one shared i. By the time the callbacks run, the loop has finished and i is 3. Using let would print 0 1 2.
The returned function keeps access to count (a closure). The first call makes it 1, the second returns 2.

body:
What does this print?

console.log([1, 2, 3] == "1,2,3");
explanation: With ==, the array is converted to the string "1,2,3" before comparing, so the values match.
Promise callbacks run after the current synchronous code, so "done" prints first, then 5 * 2 = 10.

body:
What does this print?

console.log([10, 1, 3].sort());
explanation: Without a compare function, sort() compares values as strings, and "10" comes before "3". Use sort((a, b) => a - b) for numbers.
a and b refer to the same object. const stops reassigning the variable, not changing the object's properties.

body:
What does this print?

console.log(NaN === NaN);
explanation: NaN is the only value not equal to itself. Use Number.isNaN(value) to test for it.
An async function always returns a Promise, and typeof a Promise is "object". You need await or .then() to get 7.
